svg.title: One pass of an always-on review agent
svg.desc: Left: six things that changed on a pull request since the last pass. A label, a passing check, a bot comment and a review request are read without waking the model; a maintainer's review comment and a new commit wake it. In the replays, 42% of passes with a change woke no model. Right: the agent is handed its note on the thread, what it said there before, only the news, and the diff saved to a file. Claude Code runs once with read-only tools in the clone and no GitHub token, and ends with a reply for the outbox, a question, or nothing; nothing is posted until a maintainer sends it. Measured on 76 merged pull requests from five repositories against an agent that rereads everything and keeps no memory: 0.52 times the cost, 0.41 times the drafts and 0.78 times the reviewer points raised first.
svg.text: Every 15 minutes a pass fetches what changed. Only news that asks for a
maintainer, on src/parse.rs:88: “handle the empty case”
In the replays, 42% of passes with a change asked for no response and woke
2. The model gets its memory and the news
The pass claims the news, runs the agent, files its decision, and only then
Asked: accept empty input. Said: the guard at parse.rs:88 is missing. Left: a test.
A reply draft, not yet sent by a maintainer.
Only the review comment and the commit.
Saved to a file by the pass, which it may read.
Read, Grep and Glob in the clone. No shell, no writes, no network, no GitHub
One waiting draft per thread. Nothing is posted until a maintainer sends it.
Measured on 76 merged pull requests from five repositories, against an agent with the same wakes that rereads everything and keeps no memory:
0.52× the cost, 0.41× the drafts, 0.78× the reviewer points raised first.
